machine.label: Intel Core i3-N305 laptop, 7.4 GB RAM, Linux 6.18.51-1-lts
machine.note: The same machine for every editor, shared with other running work; editors were run one at a time.

methodology: All figures were taken on one machine (see above), one editor at a time, on a freshly generated TypeScript workspace (302 files plus a 100,000-line file) with an isolated, extension-free profile per editor; each cell is the median of N runs (min and max in the tooltip) after one discarded warm-up launch. Memory is PSS (proportional set size, shared pages counted fairly) summed over the editor's whole process tree: helpers, renderers, GPU and language-server processes. Startup is the time from spawning the editor until its window shows the workspace and the first file and stops changing (screen capture polled every 100 ms), measured the same way for every editor. TypeScript timings are taken at the language-server protocol level (spawn, open a file with a type error, wait for diagnostics) with the server each editor ships. A cell marked unavailable could not be measured fairly and says why. Frame and keystroke times are only available for Lumen (CPU time of its own tests). Reproduce with tools/bench-compare.sh.

metrics.label: TypeScript: first diagnostics
metrics.description: Open src/broken.ts of a 302-file TypeScript project and wait for the first diagnostics. Measured at the language-server protocol level: Lumen runs tsgo (the native compiler); VS Code uses its bundled tsserver; Zed uses vtsls.

lumen.note: Language-server speed measured over the LSP protocol, not through the GUI: tsgo 7.0.0-dev as Lumen starts it by default (whole project, GOMEMLIMIT=512MiB GOGC=50); spawn to the first diagnostics for src/broken.ts in the 302-file sample project: median 117 ms (min 115, max 121, N=5). With the opt-in narrow mirror (lsp_narrow, loads only the open file and its imports): 66 ms, 45 MB.

vscode.note: Language-server speed measured over the LSP protocol, not through the GUI: tsserver of TypeScript 6.0.3 bundled in VS Code 1.145.2, run with VS Code's own Electron as node; spawn to the first diagnostics for src/broken.ts in the 302-file sample project: median 1186 ms (min 1167, max 1221, N=5).

zed.note: Language-server speed measured over the LSP protocol, not through the GUI: vtsls 0.3.0 (TypeScript 5.9.3), the server Zed installs for TypeScript, run with system node; spawn to the first diagnostics for src/broken.ts in the 302-file sample project: median 1763 ms (min 1628, max 1872, N=5).

sublime.reason: Sublime Text has no built-in TypeScript language server (it needs the separate LSP package plus a server), so the out-of-the-box editor has nothing to measure.

openidea.reason: No standalone TypeScript language server was identified in the install, and openidea gives no protocol endpoint to drive; not measured rather than guessed.
